speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In 2018, there was an outpouring of public concern over news of steep charges faced by hawkers in social enterprise hawker centres or SEHCs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In 2020 and 2021, there has huge public sympathy and concern for our hawkers due to dining-in restrictions; and concern over the news that some stalls had their rents raised.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And this affection that Singaporeans have for our hawkers recognises a deep reality.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Most hawkers see what they do as a calling, a calling to provide good quality, cooked food that is affordable and which deliciously combines the very best elements of Singaporean heritage and innovation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For those who want to catch the breakfast crowd, they may need to come to work at 3.00 am.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: They spend hours chopping, slicing, parsing, peeling, boiling and marinating food ingredients before any customer shows up.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And they may return home at 4.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And they work often in non-air-conditioned environments, standing up much of the time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: No wonder that attracting new entrants into the industry is an uphill climb.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I recall one story told to me by a hawker industry veteran in preparing this Adjournment Motion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: When he asked an elderly hawker why he did not raise his prices when selling to delivery apps so as to offset the app commission, the hawker said, "哪里可以", meaning, "I simply cannot bring myself to do that." Most hawkers feel a deep bond with their customers and we, to them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Our hawker culture is a heritage stretching back to the mid-1800s when street cooked food first emerged, and to 1923 when the first hawker centre at People's Park Centre was built to widespread acclaim.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: A milestone in that history, of course, was 16 December 2020 when Singapore's hawker culture was awarded a place in UNESCO's representative list for humanity's intangible cultural heritage.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In researching this Motion, I came across a speech made by a then young and new Member of Parliament, one Mr Low Thia Khiang, in 1995 asking MTI whether it foresaw the need to study the impact on hawker costs and food prices after the sale of coffee shops and market stalls in HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My speech will have three sections, three Ps, centred on the need to Protect, Professionalise and Promote the hawker industry, adapted from one of the mottos once used for the World Street Food Congress.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: All of these ideas are centred on one simple assumption: that the hawker industry should not be regulated in the same way as other industries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: As a nationally important industry and one that embodies so much of our precious national heritage, the Government and all stakeholders bear a special responsibility to go the extra mile to ensure a thriving hawker industry that retains incumbents and attracts newcomers that innovates and that continues to provide affordable food.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Above all, we have a responsibility to listen to the practitioners of the hawker craft in formulating and refining our public policies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: First of all, Sir, on the theme of "protect".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: To retain incumbents and attract newcomers, we have to create an ecosystem that allows our hawkers to make a decent living.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The policy ecosystem has to instil confidence among hawkers that there is a longer-term commitment from the Government to ensuring stable pro-hawker policies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Policies that seemed to go against this commitment, like raising rents, even if only for a small number of stalls, during a pandemic, have an outsized demonstration effect and do nothing to instil confidence.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The first subject I would like to address is rents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In its 2020 manifesto, the Workers' Party called on all hawker centres to eventually be brought under NEA control, as that would provide the necessary long-term assurance to hawkers that there are governmental levers of control over rents, not only today but also tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Social enterprises are not governmental entities and, hence, are not accountable to the public in the same way that the Government, in theory, in any case, is.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Be that as it may, I will discuss what we can do in policy terms for NEA HCs, SEHCs and privately-run HCs together.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In setting rents in the public hawker centres, I would like to argue for two principles.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For Government-controlled properties, we should never fear that some hawkers may "make too much money".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Top performers making a very decent living is a factor that attracts people into a profession.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And it is hard enough – yet vitally important – to attract young Singaporeans to the hawker trade.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In any case, the top hawkers would have put in hard work and talent to get to where they are.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This is not an industry where luck plays an outsized role.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: That is true, but the Government should use whatever levers of control it has to improve the economic situation of our hawkers and the levers are stronger for rents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Even a small difference is still a difference.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While it is said that tendering can result in extremely low rents, it does create uncertainty and can be a barrier to entry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Very low rents that may occasionally emerge from tendering also subject the hawker to a shock when the rents get raised based on the formula explained above.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: If the tendering leads to high rents – well, that favours entrants into the industry with cash rather than those with great culinary skills who may have less cash.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I would argue here that the solution need not be tendering, which favours those with more cash, nor does it have to be random balloting, the mechanism used to allocate Build-To-Order (BTO) flats and some types of subsidised hawker stalls.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such committees can bring together hawker industry veterans, enthusiasts, food critics and ordinary citizens to do blind taste tests, to decide who has the best culinary skills.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The independence of these tasting committees could be assured by being organised under the aegis of a hawker academy, a subject to which I will turn later.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Next, I want to address the plight of hawkers who operate outside of the NEA HCs and SEHCs in privately-run food courts and coffee shops.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In my Serangoon ward of Aljunied GRC, there are many hawkers in such coffee shops, many of whom are truly excellent, to the delight of constituents and their Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Hawkers in such private facilities make up the bulk of hawkers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Yet there is a perception that they do not benefit to the same extent as hawkers in NEA HCs and SEHCs from Government schemes, such as NEA rental waivers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Moreover, the Government has far less influence over the rents that they have to bear.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Government can study the plight of these so-called private hawkers in more detail, understanding their rents, margins and overall economic situation, and devise tools to nudge private operators towards cheaper rents for their tenants.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Ground feedback suggests that hawkers find the latest COVID-19 schemes, such as the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG) and COVID-19 Recovery Grant – Temporary (CRG-T), confusing and not as effective as the earlier schemes such as the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Most hawkers are micro-businesses surviving on thin profits and JSS support would mean a lot to them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Not all use and make money from delivery apps, one reason being the reluctance of some hawkers to raise prices to cover the app commissions, as I alluded to earlier.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Apps are not a panacea for the hawker industry amidst COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Also, some stalls find that they have a less compelling value proposition on apps – like drinks and dessert stalls, who depend more on dining-in.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Hence, there is a case for JSS for hawkers to cover periods of dining-in restrictions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Next, many SEHCs ensure that several stalls provide low-cost food.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Anecdotally, it would appear that some of these low-priced food stalls struggle with the customer perception that the food is not that attractive.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I believe there is such a scheme now in place, which is a special grant card for those on Public Assistance only, which can be used at certain hawker stalls, but the reach appears to be very limited.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This tool of discount cards can be expanded and made into a general policy tool to keep hawker food affordable to those on lower incomes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such discount cards may be a way in which hawker food can be priced at a level which is fair and economically sustainable for hawkers, while still keeping hawker food affordable for the poor.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Next, Sir, I would like to move to the second part of my speech, which is on professionalising the hawker industry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In framing the matter this way, I do not mean to suggest that hawkers today are not professionals, nor are they or should they be professional employees.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, by professionalising, I mean raising the status and standing of the hawker vocation, which also hinges on maintaining and raising business and culinary effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My first suggestion here would be to create a permanent pool of Hawker Ambassadors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Right now, Digital Ambassadors (DAs) under IMDA's Singapore Digital Office are deployed to hawker centres and they focus on getting hawkers to get onto digital apps and e-payments.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Anecdotal feedback suggests that the engagement of DAs with hawkers is not always very deep and is sometimes hindered by language barriers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My suggestion here is to deploy a staff of permanent Hawker Ambassadors under NEA or, perhaps, MCCY, given the heritage angle, to be deployed to all hawker centres, be they NEA HCs, SEHCs or private hawker centres (HCs).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The staffing ratio can be determined and it could be that some ambassadors cover multiple HCs, food courts and coffee shops.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Help should be focused on those hawkers who need it the most.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: On the digital front, ambassadors can work with older and less tech-savvy hawkers to help them adopt innovations, such as voice-activated systems to fulfil digital orders and to consider getting onto apps that do not charge such high commissions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Hawkers I spoke to have shared that there are too many distinct Government schemes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This is confusing, especially to hawkers who are less literate in the English language.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Ambassadors could help them identify and apply for relevant schemes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Ambassadors should also help our hawkers tell their stories and weave narratives about their history online and via events and promotions, to make their products more appealing to customers, as some larger and more organised local eateries already do.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: They could also help hawkers to connect with shared service providers who offer services such as food ingredient preparation, for example, which may be advantageous business-wise.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: One major obstacle is the mistrust that many, especially older hawkers, have towards outsiders coming along and telling them what to do.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Permanent ambassadors who can speak vernacular languages and dialects would fill this gap by building relationships with hawkers and winning their trust over time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The cost of employing such ambassadors would not be huge – in the context of the national significance of the hawker industry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Ambassador jobs could also be outsourced by the Government to NGOs, social enterprises or community groups with an interest in the well-being of hawkers, of which there are a number now, such as, for example, Hawkers United and Hawker Cart.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Over time, as a more digitally savvy generation of hawkers takes over, permanent ambassadors could be phased out if there is no need for them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I would also like to call for the Competition and Consumer Commission to take pains to act as a good watchdog over the delivery app industry, to ensure fair competition between the big app companies and smaller ones that charge low or no commissions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Right now, there is a hawker course run at Temasek Polytechnic and a course at ITE.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: These could be consolidated under a single hawker academy, which could become a focal point for the hawker vocation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: An independent hawker academy could be a one-stop shop for training of various kinds – culinary and business.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It could be a think tank that supports research into hawker-related policies and issues.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It could support the efforts of hawkers to innovate and create new dishes or business models.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It could also, being seen to be independent, be tasked to convene and supervise the tasting committees to allocate stalls when there are excess bidders.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such an academy could even aspire to play a leading role in organising events and research for the global street food industry, which could yield soft power and economic benefits to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, Sir, I will move on to the third and last section of my speech on the need to "promote".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: We should do more to support and nurture the best-performing and most innovative hawkers to go global.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some hawkers are more successful and ambitious, operating multiple stalls across the island.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It would be a huge boost for our hawker culture and for Singapore's soft power if these hawkers set up successful eateries abroad.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This would raise awareness of and esteem for Singaporean culture abroad, which can only be a good thing.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some of these more ambitious hawkers could also obtain economic benefits from overseas operations, resulting in multiplier benefits back to the Singapore economy.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Why is Singapore food not as widely enjoyed around the world as, say, Japanese or Thai food?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Not for any reasons to do with quality, I am sure.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In fact, I understand that the late global celebrity chef Anthony Bourdain wanted to bring some Singaporean hawkers and other hawkers from around the world to New York for a global event on street food.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And I am told that he felt that the Singaporean hawkers were among the very best practitioners of street food in the world.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: With the proper support system and with the support of the over 200,000 Singaporeans living abroad, I do not see why we cannot have prata in Paris, lontong in London, bak kut teh in Belgrade or rojak in Rio De Janeiro.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It is a deep part of Singapore's heritage and now the world's as well.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In moving this Motion, it is not my intention to say that we have not made progress over the decades in nurturing this industry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It is to point out gaps and offer suggestions for how we can do right by this nationally important industry and the hawkers whom we all care about, who work so hard to bring us incredible, delicious food at affordable prices day after day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, our hawker trade is a key part of Singapore's history and identity, very much loved and treasured by Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The inscription of our hawker culture by UNESCO is a proud achievement for all hawkers and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To ensure that the hawker trade and culture continue to thrive for future generations, we have been working closely with hawkers and stakeholders to, as Mr Leon Perera said, professionalise the trade, improve working conditions and keep barriers to entry low.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We work closely with the hawker community to support new hawkers and encourage existing hawkers to adapt to changes, as we future-proof our hawkers and hawker trade, that is, to protect and to promote them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Eligible hawkers also received $9,000 under the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Those who continue to face financial difficulties can reach out to NEA and we will review the case and provide assistance on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Stallholders in other F&B establishments, coffee shops and food courts have also been supported during this pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Stallholders that contribute CPF for their employees from October 2019 would have received 17 months of wage support under the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During this recent Phase Two (Heightened Alert), eligible stallholders in Government-owned commercial properties will receive one-month rental relief and those in privately-owned commercial properties will receive two weeks' rental relief.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To help F&B operators, Enterprise Singapore has reintroduced the Food Delivery Booster Package for the Phase Two (Heightened Alert) period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Eligible stallholders can also apply for financial support under the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government is committed to supporting our hawkers as well as stallholders in other F&B establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation and assess the need for further assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Mr Perera is well aware, food courts and coffeeshops are operated commercially by private operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Stallholders and the F&B operators enter willingly into commercial arrangements after assessing the business potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Regardless, anyone aspiring to become hawkerpreneurs always has the option of securing a stall in NEA centres which are open to all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is because of policies such as doing away with the minimum bid price through tender, which is the most transparent manner of allocation of such stalls, to allow hawker centres to serve as our community dining rooms while ensuring that hawkers can earn a decent livelihood, even as they provide affordable food for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres, or SEHC operators, will ensure, not just a few, but each of every stall in the centres sells at least one item priced $3 and below.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This provides affordable options while allowing hawkers to provide diverse food offerings and sell additional items with higher profit margin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The SEHC model is working well and has benefited hawkers and patrons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Average occupancy rates at SEHCs remained high at 98% in June 2021, with very little turnover.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Operating costs, including rentals, are on par with comparable existing centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During this pandemic, operators have demonstrated their useful role by helping their hawkers adopt online food delivery and curating activities to attract footfall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond COVID-19, we must ensure our hawker culture and food continue to thrive for future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have been working closely with hawkers and stakeholders to sustain the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Building on veteran hawkers' advice – so we talk to the hawkers constantly – we have taken steps to provide new hawkers with necessary skillsets to boost their chances of succeeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Aspiring hawkers can also participate in NEA's Incubation Stall Programme (ISP), which provides up to 15 months' rental subsidies and fitted-out stalls to lower start-up costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To date, 92 aspiring hawkers have participated in these programmes, with 38 becoming full-fledged hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The median age of these hawkerpreneurs is 36.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To help sustain the hawker trade and heritage, we are piloting the Hawkers Succession Scheme (HSS) to help retiring veteran hawkers pass down culinary skills, recipes as well as stalls to aspiring successors through an apprenticeship and mentorship programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: COVID-19 has presented learning points on future-proofing our hawker centres and hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To make hawker centres cleaner, safer and more productive, we introduced the Hawker Centres Transformation Programme (HTP), which will include improvements such as better aisles and tables spacing to minimise crowding, and high-volume-low-speed fans to improve ventilation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also encourage hawker centres to get onto the Productive Hawker Centres (PHC) programme and adopt automated tray return systems and centralised dishwashing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To help hawkers enhance business resiliency, the Hawkers' Productivity Grant (HPG) co-funds the purchase of equipment to streamline business processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The pandemic has brought to the fore online food delivery for hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While this is no silver bullet, it is one way to help hawkers boost their revenue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There is, however, no easy or one-size-fits-all solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hawkers have different needs and preferences, and not all hawker food is suitable for food delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond the larger delivery platforms, there are various others that hawkers can work with, such as WhyQ and Bungkus, and each adopts a different business model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some provide onsite support to manage online orders and some have different fee structures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some charge hawkers little or no commission, with costs borne by consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Each model has its benefits and targets different segments of hawkers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This aims to address challenges hawkers face in using delivery services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The AfA will look at raising hawkers' awareness and understanding of different platforms, facilitate their onboarding and equip them with means to successfully market their food online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It will also explore more sustainable platform costs for both hawkers and patrons by exploring different business models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Meanwhile, our Digital Ambassadors from SG Digital Office will continue to support hawkers by helping them get onboard e-payment and online delivery platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We aim to develop an ecosystem of support, where all hawkers – tech-savvy or otherwise – can join if they wish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We can all do our part to keep hawker centres vibrant and safe by patronising our hawker stalls online or offline, and adhering to Safe Management Measures, as well as, of course, clearing our trays and dirty crockeries and litter up when dine-in resumes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Deep-cleaning and disinfection of affected centres have been carried out, and we have also implemented access control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will continue to work with stakeholders but, ultimately, it is up to all Singaporeans to support our hawkers to ensure that our hawker trade and culture continue to thrive.
